subject.name: Travel and Tourism
subject.description: Travel and Tourism syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

topics.name: TOPIC 1.3: MOTIVATION IN TOURISM
topics.description: Motivation in Tourism is a fundamental concept that drives individuals to engage in travel, whether for relaxation, adventure, learning, or cultural exploration. Understanding travel motivations helps the tourism sector design better travel experiences, services, and marketing strategies to meet tourist expectations.

sub_topics.name: Sub-Topic 1.3.1: Motivation to Travel
sub_topics.description: This sub-topic introduces learners to the concept of travel motivation, exploring why people travel, factors influencing travel decisions, activities that encourage travel, different types of motivators, and how to analyze travel trends through community surveys.

topics.name: 1.4 TOURISM PRODUCTS AND SERVICES
topics.description: The tourism industry revolves around creating memorable experiences rather than selling physical goods. This module introduces learners to the core elements of tourism products and services, including transport, accommodation, food and beverage, attractions, activities, and supportive services, as well as their unique characteristics such as intangibility, inseparability, variability, and perishability.
learning_objectives: Discuss key characteristics of tourism products and services (intangibility, inseparability, variability, perishability, etc.).
Categorize natural and man-made attraction centers in Zambia and evaluate their significance.

competencies.description: Analytical Thinking: Analysing various components of tourism products and services.
Creativity and Innovation: Designing or proposing appealing and marketable tourism products and services that suit different customer preferences and destinations.
Critical Thinking: Evaluating the effectiveness of tourism products and services in different contexts.
Problem-Solving: Suggesting improvements or alternatives for better tourist Satisfaction.
Communication: Ability to describe and explain the characteristics of tourism products and services clearly (intangibility, inseparability, variability).

sub_topics.name: 1.4.1 Products and Services in Tourism
sub_topics.description: Focuses on analyzing types of tourism products and services, examining their defining service characteristics, and classifying natural and man-made tourist attraction centers across Zambia.
learning_objectives: Analyse tourism products (transport, accommodation, food and beverage, activities, travel packages) and services (travel insurance, formalities, communication, booking, safety, tour services).
Discuss the key characteristics of tourism products and services using real-life scenarios, role-play simulations, and guest speakers.

Categorize natural attraction centers (national parks, waterfalls, rivers, mountains, etc.) and man-made attraction centers (museums, dams, wildlife sanctuaries, historical monuments, etc.) and research their significance in Zambia.
